fields.name: feed_id

fields.name: publish_time
docs: The timestamp of this price update in seconds

fields.name: prev_publish_time
docs: The timestamp of the previous price update. This field is intended to allow users to
identify the single unique price update for any moment in time:
for any time t, the unique update is the one such that prev_publish_time < t <= publish_time.
Note that there may not be such an update while we are migrating to the new message-sending logic,
as some price updates on pythnet may not be sent to other chains (because the message-sending
logic may not have triggered). We can solve this problem by making the message-sending mandatory
(which we can do once publishers have migrated over).
Additionally, this field may be equal to publish_time if the message is sent on a slot where
where the aggregation was unsuccesful. This problem will go away once all publishers have
migrated over to a recent version of pyth-agent.

types.name: PriceSource
docs: Where the token spot price is read from.

types.name: PriceUpdateV2
docs: A price update account. This account is used by the Pyth Receiver program to store a verified price update from a Pyth price feed.
It contains:
- `write_authority`: The write authority for this account. This authority can close this account to reclaim rent or update the account to contain a different price update.
- `verification_level`: The [`VerificationLevel`] of this price update. This represents how many Wormhole guardian signatures have been verified for this price update.
- `price_message`: The actual price update.
- `posted_slot`: The slot at which this price update was posted.

fields.name: spot
docs: lamports per token base unit * 1e18

fields.name: ema
docs: lamports per token base unit * 1e18

fields.name: slow_ema
docs: slow (4 h) EMA, same unit

types.name: VerificationLevel
docs: Pyth price updates are bridged to all blockchains via Wormhole.
Using the price updates on another chain requires verifying the signatures of the Wormhole guardians.
The usual process is to check the signatures for two thirds of the total number of guardians, but this can be cumbersome on Solana because of the transaction size limits,
so we also allow for partial verification.
This enum represents how much a price update has been verified:
- If `Full`, we have verified the signatures for two thirds of the current guardians.
- If `Partial`, only `num_signatures` guardian signatures have been checked.
# Warning
Using partially verified price updates is dangerous, as it lowers the threshold of guardians that need to collude to produce a malicious price update.

constants.name: AD_AUCTION_SEED
docs: The single final-auction ad: ["ad_auction"].

constants.name: AD_SEED
docs: Rect ads: ["ad", top-left block index u16 LE]. Blocks are exclusive, so the address is unique per ad and
independent of global state (no collisions between concurrent buyers of disjoint rects).

constants.name: AUCTION_EXTENSION_SECS
docs: A bid inside the last 10 minutes pushes the end to now + 10 minutes (anti-sniping).

constants.name: BUYBACK_MAX_POST_SPOT_BPS
docs: Backstop checked in `record_buyback_burn` (spent > 0): spot must be <= fast EMA * (1 + 12%), 3 points inside the
15% token-buy band, so the keeper's atomic release -> swap -> record flow cannot push spot past fast EMA * 1.12.
This is a safety rail for the honest keeper, NOT an adversarial control: nothing on-chain ties the record to the
swap (same as the rate bar), so a malicious keeper could swap in a separate transaction.

constants.name: DEFAULT_TOKEN_BLOCKS_CAP_PER_HOUR
docs: Hard ceiling and default for the token-payment rate limit (blocks per hour, token bucket).

constants.name: EMA_ALPHA_BPS
docs: Fixed per-crank alpha = 30/600 = 5%.

constants.name: EMA_MAX_DEVIATION_BPS
docs: Token buys are rejected while spot > fast EMA * (1 + 15%) (one-sided; spot below the EMA is allowed).

constants.name: EMA_SEED_BAND_BPS
docs: The admin-supplied EMA seed must be within 25% of spot at the first crank after seeding.

constants.name: EMA_SPOT_CLAMP_BPS
docs: Spot input is clamped to EMA * (1 +/- 40%) before the alpha step, so one crank moves the EMA by at most
5% * 40% = 2% (MAX_EMA_STEP_BPS), and cranks are >= 30 s apart: <= 2% per 30 s.

constants.name: EMA_WARMUP_CRANKS
docs: Warm-up after seeding: token buys / keeper reconciliation need >= 10 cranks spanning >= 600 s.

constants.name: EMA_WINDOW_SECS
docs: Nominal EMA time constant. Each crank uses the FIXED alpha EMA_MIN_INTERVAL_SECS / EMA_WINDOW_SECS (5%),
regardless of how long ago the previous crank was (a long gap never lets one crank jump to spot).

constants.name: GRID
docs: Blocks per side (1000 px / 10 px).

constants.name: MAX_CONF_BPS
docs: Reject Pyth prices whose confidence interval exceeds 2% of the price.

constants.name: MAX_EMA_AGE_SECS
docs: `buy_with_token` refuses to price against an EMA older than this.

constants.name: MAX_PRICE_AGE_LIMIT_SECS
docs: Upper bound the admin can configure for the Pyth staleness window.

constants.name: PRICE_PER_BLOCK_USD_MICRO
docs: $100 per 10x10 block, micro-USD (6 decimals).

constants.name: SLOW_EMA_WINDOW_SECS
docs: Slow EMA (audit round 2, ratchet fix): 4-hour window, alpha = 30 s / 14_400 s = 1/480 per crank, same ±40% clamp,
so it moves at most 0.0833% per crank (~ +10.5% per hour of a held +40% pump). Token price = min(spot, fast, slow).

constants.name: TOKEN_DISCOUNT_BPS
docs: Discount for paying in the token.

constants.name: TOKEN_SYMBOL
docs: Ticker placeholder. The only place in the program that names the token.

constants.name: TREASURY_BPS
docs: Share of SOL payments sent to the treasury. The remainder (incl. rounding dust) goes to the buyback vault.
